messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Burns <caroline.burns@finexanalytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity increment validation and ops transition

Hi Caroline / Samir —

Thanks again for signing the renewal and committing to the additional 8 A100 GPUs in the dedicated pool. Per our agreement the new capacity is scheduled for the week of Feb 15 and Marcus ran the validation plan over the weekend. I wanted to share the short summary and propose acceptance criteria so we can close the loop on the amendment and hand the space to your SREs.

What we validated (summary):
- Capacity provisioned: +8 A100 GPUs (reserved pool) attached to finex-prod-dedicated.
- Peak concurrent streams: sustained 1,800 streams for 30m at median p99 latency 230ms.
- Autoscale/overcommit checks: burst headroom of ~12% observed for 2m spikes.

Acceptance checklist proposed (please confirm):
1) Latency SLA: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 300ms under steady-state throughput (1,500 streams).
2) Throughput: sustain 1,600 tokens/sec across pool for 30m.
3) Failover: cross-region fallback to eu-1 disabled for this reserved pool (per contract).
4) Monitoring handoff: Redwood to provide ops runbook and Grafana dashboard links; Finex to confirm alert recipients.

Marcus has a short load report attached with the raw traces. Once you confirm the acceptance items I can send the DocuSign amendment and we’ll schedule a 30-minute ops transfer with your platform team.

Next steps: please reply with either (A) acceptance as-is, (B) acceptance with scope edits, or (C) list of specific fail items.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
-----

Diego —

Thanks for the summary; appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications before sign-off:

- p99 at 230ms under 1,800 streams looks good, but can you share the distribution by model? Our workload mixes long-context and short prompts; we care about the 8k-context routing.
- Is the autoscale headroom guaranteed for sustained spikes longer than 2m? We want to understand throttling behavior if there’s a burst after midnight.
- Please confirm the retention window for KV cache metrics (we need 90 days).

If those items look ok we should be able to sign the amendment this week. Also include the DocuSign link in the next message.

—Caroline
Caroline Burns
Head of Platform Engineering | Finex Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Burns <caroline.burns@finexanalytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexanalytics.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity increment validation and ops transition

Caroline — quick answers + attached deeper traces. Forwarding the relevant excerpts from the weekend run: 

- Model breakdown: 65% small-chat (8k truncation), 25% assistant-long (32k with quantized kernels), 10% rerank. p99 by model: small-chat 210ms, assistant-long 420ms (but note the assistant-long p95 ~240ms at 32k). The long-context paths use the quantized lane which increases p99 slightly.
- Autoscale headroom: the reserved pool is configured with proactive reserved capacity + soft-burst to the shared capacity tier. Soft-burst is ~12% for short spikes; for sustained spikes >5m we start queuing at the gateway per policy. If you need guaranteed 5m burst we can extend the reserved cushion (we’ve done that for a few customers).
- KV cache metrics: Redwood retains per-request KV hit/miss aggregates for 90 days by default for Dedicated; raw KV trace retention is 30 days unless you enable extended telemetry (we can enable 90d per your compliance).

I’ve attached the raw CSV traces and a condensed chart.

Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity increment validation and ops transition

Marcus / Diego / Caroline —

Thanks for the details. We’ve reviewed with our SREs (quick sync this morning):
- The model-specific numbers look acceptable; the assistant-long p99 is higher than ideal but within our risk tolerance for now.
- We want to add a 5-minute guaranteed burst cushion for peak ETL windows. Can Redwood provide a formal addendum to the amendment for a temporary 5-minute burst guarantee (we’ll revert to standard after 90 days)?
- Please confirm you will enable 90-day KV raw trace retention for finex-prod-dedicated for the next 90 days.

If Redwood can confirm both items we will sign and route the amendment to legal.

Samir
Sr. Platform SRE | Finex Analytics

Caroline / Samir —

Short update: Redwood will deliver the requested items and this email serves as formal acceptance and next steps from our side. Details below: 

1) Temporary burst cushion: Redwood can add a 5-minute guaranteed burst cushion of +16% capacity for finex-prod-dedicated for a 90-day period starting Feb 18. We will document this in the DocuSign amendment and set an automatic rollback on May 18.
2) KV raw trace retention: enabled for 90 days starting Feb 16; logs and raw KV traces will be available under the Finex telemetry project in our retention tier.
3) DocuSign: amendment sent — https://docusign.com/link/to/FINEX_CAPACITY_AMENDMENT (signed by Finex once you click through)
4) Ops handoff: I’ve attached the ops runbook and set up a 30-minute transfer call for Feb 19 at 11:00 PST. Link: https://meet.redwood.ai/ops-transfer/finex (Marcus will lead the run-through).

Acceptance sign-off: Caroline, Samir — please reply with an explicit acceptance reply (email confirmation is fine). After we receive that I will mark the amendment complete and update the deal stage in HubSpot.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth transition.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
